title: A divisibility argument and its converse
stem: For an integer $n$, define $D=n^3-n$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorize $D$ and prove that it is divisible by 6 for every integer $n$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A student claims: “If an integer is divisible by 6, it must equal $n^3-n$ for some integer $n$.” Disprove the claim using the integer 12.

steps.text: Of three consecutive integers, at least one is even.
Exactly one of the three is divisible by 3; together these factors give divisibility by 6.
For positive integers $n$, the successive difference is $3n(n+1)>0$; no positive integer gives a value between 6 and 24.
